items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this as a popular geography YouTube Shorts channel explaining a news story with a map. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller: brisk and curious, natural emphasis on numbers, a short comic pause before each punchline, slightly hushed and serious on the 'strangest part' line. Chars voices a giant mountain range as a funny cartoon character: slow, deep, smug and deadpan.
lines: Narrator
This week, eighty-six of the world's hundred most polluted cities were in one country.
Narrator
One Delhi station hit four hundred eighty-eight. The scale stops at five hundred.
Narrator
So why here? From space, it's a grey river... Punjab to Bengal.
Narrator
Four in ten Indians live under it.
Narrator
Because north India is a giant bowl.
Narrator
North: the tallest wall on Earth.
Chars
[smug, slow, deep] Nothing gets past me. Not even smoke.
Narrator
South: the Aravalli and Vindhya hills.
Narrator
But it's been a bowl for millions of years. So why only in winter?
Narrator
In summer, warm air rises about a kilometre... and takes the smoke away.
Narrator
In November, cold air slides off the Tibetan Plateau... and warm air sits on top.
Narrator
Like a lid on a pot.
Narrator
The ceiling drops to a few hundred metres... and the wind goes quiet.
Narrator
And that's still not the strangest part.
Narrator
Researchers say, even if Delhi made zero pollution itself...
Narrator
its winter air would likely still turn bad.
Narrator
Because smoke from farms, roads and factories across the plain shares one sky.
Narrator
Air doesn't stop at city lines.
Chars
[deadpan, defensive] Don't look at me. I'm just tall.
Narrator
Comment your city's A-Q-I right now.
Narrator
This is Bhoogol. Follow for more Geography Fun Facts.
